sudan.title: الجيش يعلن إحباط هجوم لـ«الدعم السريع والشعبية» بالنيل الأزرق - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: أعلن الجيش السوداني عن إحباط هجوم لمجموعتي "الدعم السريع" و"الشعبية" في ولاية النيل الأزرق. وأكد المتحدث باسم الجيش أن القوات المسلحة تصدت للهجوم، مما أدى إلى وقوع اشتباكات عنيفة بين الطرفين. وأوضح أن الجيش تمكن من استعادة السيطرة على المناطق التي تعرضت للهجوم، مشيراً إلى أن الوضع تحت السيطرة. كما أشار إلى أن القوات المسلحة ستواصل عملياتها لحماية الأمن والاستقرار في المنطقة. يأتي هذا التطور في ظل تصاعد التوترات بين القوات المسلحة والمجموعات المسلحة في السودان.

sudan.title: ارتفاع قياسي جديد في سعر الدولار الجمركي بالسودان - سودان اندبندنت
sudan.summary: سجل سعر الدولار الجمركي في السودان ارتفاعًا قياسيًا جديدًا، حيث بلغ 9,000 جنيه سوداني. يأتي هذا الارتفاع في ظل الأوضاع الاقتصادية الصعبة التي يواجهها البلد، بما في ذلك التضخم المتزايد ونقص العملات الأجنبية. الحكومة السودانية تسعى إلى معالجة هذه التحديات من خلال تعديل السياسات الاقتصادية، لكن تأثير هذه الإجراءات على السوق لا يزال غير واضح. يثير هذا الارتفاع قلق التجار والمستهلكين، حيث من المتوقع أن يؤدي إلى زيادة أسعار السلع والخدمات.

sudan.title: قفزة قياسية جديدة بسعر الدولار الجمركي في السودان - العربية
sudan.summary: سجل سعر الدولار الجمركي في السودان قفزة قياسية جديدة، حيث ارتفع إلى 15,000 جنيه سوداني. يأتي هذا الارتفاع في ظل الأزمات الاقتصادية المتزايدة التي يعاني منها البلد، بما في ذلك التضخم المرتفع ونقص العملات الأجنبية. الحكومة السودانية تسعى إلى معالجة هذه التحديات من خلال تعديل سعر الدولار الجمركي، مما يؤثر على أسعار السلع المستوردة ويزيد من الضغوط على المواطنين. هذا التغيير يعكس الوضع الاقتصادي الصعب الذي يواجهه السودان، ويثير مخاوف من تأثيره على القدرة الشرائية للمواطنين.

sudan.title: ريبورتاج - اللاجئون السودانيون في جنوب السودان.. حين تتراجع المساعدات وتتسع الاحتياجات - مونت كارلو الدولية
sudan.summary: تتناول المقالة وضع اللاجئين السودانيين في جنوب السودان، حيث تزايدت احتياجاتهم في ظل تراجع المساعدات الإنسانية. يعاني هؤلاء اللاجئون من ظروف معيشية صعبة، بما في ذلك نقص الغذاء والرعاية الصحية، مما يزيد من معاناتهم. تشير التقارير إلى أن العديد من المنظمات الإنسانية تواجه صعوبات في تقديم الدعم اللازم بسبب نقص التمويل. كما يتطرق المقال إلى التحديات التي يواجهها اللاجئون في التكيف مع الحياة في جنوب السودان، بما في ذلك التوترات الاجتماعية والاقتصادية. في ظل هذه الظروف، يبقى الأمل في تحسين الوضع مع زيادة الوعي الدولي وضرورة تقديم المساعدات اللازمة.

sudan.title: السودان الجديد وشرعية التمثيل: مرة أخرى مع خالد كودي - سودان تربيون

sudan.title: الجيش السوداني يسقط مسيرات لـ«الدعم السريع» في محيط مطار الخرطوم - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: أسقط الجيش السوداني طائرات مسيرة تابعة لقوات الدعم السريع في محيط مطار الخرطوم. وأكدت مصادر عسكرية أن هذه العملية تأتي في إطار التصدي للتهديدات الأمنية التي تمثلها هذه الطائرات. وقد شهدت المنطقة توترات متزايدة بين الجيش السوداني وقوات الدعم السريع، مما أدى إلى تصعيد العمليات العسكرية. يأتي هذا التطور في وقت حساس، حيث يسعى الجيش للحفاظ على السيطرة الأمنية في العاصمة.

sudan.title: الجيش يتصدى لمسيّرات في الخرطوم.. تابعة للدعم السريع - العربية
sudan.summary: تصدى الجيش السوداني لمسيّرات تابعة لقوات الدعم السريع في العاصمة الخرطوم. وقد تم رصد هذه الطائرات المسيرة أثناء محاولتها تنفيذ عمليات فوق مناطق مختلفة من المدينة. وأكدت مصادر عسكرية أن الدفاعات الجوية للجيش تمكنت من إسقاط عدد من هذه الطائرات، مما أدى إلى تفادي أي أضرار محتملة. يأتي هذا التصدي في إطار الصراع المستمر بين الجيش وقوات الدعم السريع، حيث تتزايد التوترات في البلاد. وقد دعا الجيش إلى ضرورة تعزيز الأمن والاستقرار في الخرطوم، مشدداً على استعداده لمواجهة أي تهديدات.

sudan.title: البرهان خارج حسابات الوسطاء.. جنيف تعيد رسم مسار التسوية السودانية - إرم نيوز
sudan.summary: تتجه الأنظار إلى جنيف حيث يتم إعادة رسم مسار التسوية في السودان، مع استبعاد قائد الجيش السوداني، عبد الفتاح البرهان، من حسابات الوسطاء. تأتي هذه التطورات في وقت حساس، حيث يسعى المجتمع الدولي إلى إيجاد حل للأزمة السياسية المستمرة في البلاد. الوساطة الدولية تأمل في تحقيق تقدم من خلال الحوار بين الأطراف المعنية، رغم التحديات الكبيرة التي تواجهها. يُعتبر هذا التحول في التركيز على جنيف خطوة مهمة نحو تحقيق الاستقرار في السودان، في ظل الظروف الراهنة التي تعاني منها البلاد.

sudan.title: إدارة ترامب تصدر قرارا جديدا بشأن المهاجرين من السودان وأوكرانيا - CNN Arabic
sudan.summary: أصدرت إدارة ترامب قرارًا جديدًا يتعلق بالمهاجرين من السودان وأوكرانيا، حيث يهدف القرار إلى تسهيل إجراءات الهجرة لهؤلاء الأفراد. يأتي هذا القرار في إطار جهود الإدارة لدعم الأشخاص الذين فروا من النزاعات والأزمات في بلدانهم. يتضمن القرار توفير فرص للجوء وإعادة التوطين، مما يعكس التزام الحكومة الأمريكية بمساعدة المهاجرين الذين يعانون من ظروف صعبة. كما يتوقع أن يسهم هذا القرار في تحسين وضع المهاجرين ويمنحهم فرصة لبداية جديدة في الولايات المتحدة.

sudan.title: تصعيد حرب المسيرات في السودان وسيطرة الجيش على 63% من البلاد - جريدة القدس
sudan.summary: تشهد السودان تصعيدًا في استخدام الطائرات المسيرة في النزاع المستمر بين الجيش السوداني وقوات الدعم السريع. وفقًا لتقارير، تمكن الجيش من السيطرة على 63% من أراضي البلاد، مما يعكس تقدمه في الصراع. يأتي هذا التصعيد في وقت تتزايد فيه الضغوط الدولية للتهدئة ووقف الأعمال العدائية. بينما تستمر المعارك في مناطق مختلفة، يعاني المدنيون من تداعيات النزاع، بما في ذلك نقص الموارد الأساسية والتهجير. الوضع الإنساني في البلاد يتدهور، مما يستدعي استجابة عاجلة من المجتمع الدولي.

ethiopia.title: Nile and Red Sea Inseparable Pillars Capable of Creating Regional Cooperation, Integration: Researchers - ENA English
ethiopia.summary: Researchers have emphasized the interconnectedness of the Nile and Red Sea as vital components for fostering regional cooperation and integration in East Africa. They argue that these two bodies of water are not only crucial for the ecological and economic stability of the region but also serve as platforms for collaborative initiatives among neighboring countries. By leveraging the resources and strategic significance of the Nile and Red Sea, nations can enhance trade, address environmental challenges, and promote sustainable development. The researchers advocate for a unified approach to managing these waterways, highlighting the potential benefits of regional partnerships in achieving long-term stability and prosperity.

ethiopia.title: Ugandans in Ethiopia Called to Contribute to Country's Growth Through Investment, Trade and Skills Transfer
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Ugandans in Ethiopia Called to Contribute to Country's Growth Through Investment, Trade and Skills Transfer - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Ugandans in Ethiopia Called to Contribute to Country's Growth Through Investment, Trade and Skills Transfer 19 October 2026 The Independent (Kampala) Addis Ababa — Uganda convened its diaspora community in Ethiopia for a two-day event at the Hilton Addis Ababa, centered on "Connecting, Celebrating and Contributing: Harnessing the Ugandan Diaspora for National Development." The forum aimed to strengthen ties between Ugandans living in Ethiopia and national development priorities, while showcasing Uganda's culture, investment opportunities, and talent to a global audience. The Ugandan community in Ethiopia is composed of a diverse and influential network, including professionals, students, business people, families, researchers, and staff from regional and international organizations. Ethiopia's status as a hub for the African Union and numerous NGOs provides a unique setting for diaspora engagement, enabling participants to tap into valuable professional networks, to exchange knowledge, and explore cross-border business opportunities. Speaking at a dinner hosted by the Uganda Embassy, Amb. Rebecca Amuge Otengo, Ambassador of Uganda to Ethiopia welcomed the guests and delivered the best wishes of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni. She emphasized that their presence in Ethiopia is important. Pointing out that through their professional work, businesses, studies and daily interactions, they contribute to Uganda's image and to the longstanding friendship between Uganda and Ethiopia. She encouraged them to continue conducting themselves with integrity, respecting the laws and customs of the host country, and contributing positively to the communities in which they live and work. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines "As we pursue opportunities abroad, let us never forget home. Our families, communities and country remain an important part of who we are. I encourage you to maintain close contact with your families, remain informed about developments in Uganda and, whenever circumstances permit, visit home and explore opportunities to contribute to our national development." said, Otengo "The development of our country is a shared responsibility. Each of us has something to contribute, whether through professional expertise, new ideas, investment, enterprise or support to our families and communities. Let us turn our presence in Ethiopia into an opportunity to deepen Uganda-Ethiopia relations, promote shared prosperity and contribute to Uganda's transformation." Wondafrash Debere Tolera who represented Amb Zerihun Abebe, Director-General for African Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Federal Republic of Ethiopia at the dinner addressed the Ugandan Community and hailed them for the being exemplary in behavior and for their developmental approach while living in Ethiopia. Mr Tolera emphasized the importance of people-to-people ties, hailing the growing Ethiopian Community in the Kampala suburbs of Muyenga, Kansanga and Buziga which has now acquired the moniker 'Little Ethiopia". He said they would like to see the warm reception given to the Ethiopian people, grow into a thriving commercial and business relationship. The forum, titled "Connecting, Celebrating and Contributing," aimed to strengthen connections between the Ugandan diaspora and national development priorities while promoting Uganda's culture and investment opportunities. Ambassador Rebecca Amuge Otengo emphasized the importance of the diaspora's role in enhancing Uganda's image and fostering Uganda-Ethiopia relations. Ethiopian officials praised the Ugandan community for their positive contributions and behavior in Ethiopia, highlighting the potential for deeper commercial ties.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement 19 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — The Ethiopian high-level delegation met with Eric Meyer, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Africa and the Middle East at the U.S. Department of the Treasury, on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok. According to the social media post by National Bank of Ethiopia, the high-level engagement focused on exploring expanded avenues of technical and financial support, including within international financial institutions, to help sustain and accelerate Ethiopia's ongoing economic reforms. The two sides also exchanged views on political and security developments in the region. During the session, Deputy Assistant Secretary Meyer commended Ethiopia's commitment to structural economic reforms and underscored the United States' continued dedication to a constructive bilateral partnership. Both delegations concluded the meeting by agreeing to maintain regular, constructive dialogue to advance mutual development goals and foster regional stability. Read the original article on ENA . ethiopia.title: Ethiopia's civil war threatens wider conflict as Somaliland offers Addis Ababa a route to the sea - i24NEWS
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia's ongoing civil war poses a risk of escalating into a broader regional conflict, particularly as tensions rise in the Horn of Africa. Somaliland has extended an offer to Ethiopia, proposing to provide a route to the sea, which could enhance trade and access for the landlocked nation. This development comes amid increasing instability in Ethiopia, where clashes between government forces and Tigrayan rebels have persisted. The potential for Somaliland's involvement highlights the complex geopolitical dynamics in the region, as neighboring countries monitor the situation closely. Analysts warn that if the conflict spreads, it could have significant implications for regional security and economic stability.

ethiopia.title: Eritrea’s Incursion and Ethiopia’s Right to Self-Defense: Where Does the Law Stand? - horn review
ethiopia.summary: The article discusses the legal implications of Eritrea's military actions against Ethiopia and Ethiopia's right to self-defense under international law. It examines the context of the conflict, highlighting Eritrea's incursions and the historical tensions between the two nations. The piece analyzes relevant legal frameworks, including the United Nations Charter, which allows for self-defense in response to armed attacks. Additionally, it considers the potential consequences of Ethiopia's military response and the international community's role in addressing the situation. The article emphasizes the need for a balanced understanding of the legal rights and responsibilities of both nations amidst ongoing hostilities.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia’s Intellectual Crisis Begins With a Culture of Conformity - Ethiopia Insight
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia is facing an intellectual crisis rooted in a pervasive culture of conformity that stifles critical thinking and innovation. This environment discourages open dialogue and the questioning of established norms, leading to a lack of diverse perspectives in academic and public discourse. The article highlights how this conformity affects various sectors, including education and governance, ultimately hindering the country's development. It emphasizes the need for fostering a culture that encourages independent thought and creativity to address pressing societal challenges. By promoting intellectual freedom and critical engagement, Ethiopia can cultivate a more dynamic and progressive society capable of tackling its complex issues.

ethiopia.title: African Diplomats Urge Stronger African-Led Strategies, Sustained Dialogue, Local Ownership, Adequate Financing
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: African Diplomats Urge Stronger African-Led Strategies, Sustained Dialogue, Local Ownership, Adequate Financing - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: African Diplomats Urge Stronger African-Led Strategies, Sustained Dialogue, Local Ownership, Adequate Financing 18 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — African diplomats have called for stronger African-led strategies to address the continent's conflicts and security challenges. Approached by Pulse of Africa at the Pre-Tana Forum Dialogue in Bahir Dar, the ambassadors emphasized that sustained dialogue, local ownership and adequate financing are essential to achieving lasting peace and development. Ghana's Ambassador to Ethiopia, McArios Akanbeanab Akanbong, and Burundi's Permanent Representative to the African Union, Ambassador Willy Nyamitwe, highlighted the importance of platforms that bring together policymakers, diplomats, academics and civil society representatives to develop solutions grounded in Africa's realities. Ambassador Akanbong said the Tana Forum provides an important platform for Africa to shape its security agenda, examine the root causes of conflict and formulate strategies to address terrorism, interstate tensions and other threats to stability. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The Ghanaian ambassador also said that heavy reliance on external financing could leave Africa vulnerable to outside influence. While acknowledging the importance of international partnerships, he stressed that such cooperation should reinforce, rather than undermine, African ownership of the continent's priorities and solutions. Meanwhile, Ambassador Nyamitwe called for sustained efforts to achieve the African Union's goal of silencing the guns by 2030. He said continued dialogue was necessary to assess setbacks, bring diverse stakeholders together and identify practical pathways toward peace. Nyamitwe also highlighted the close link between security and economic development, noting that sustainable progress depends on peaceful and stable societies. He added that Burundi, under the chairmanship of its president at the African Union, remained committed to advancing peace and security alongside broader development priorities, including water and sanitation, education, youth empowerment and women's advancement. Held under the theme "Navigating a Changing World: The Role of Diplomacy and Dialogue in Advancing Peace and Security in Africa," the Pre-Tana Forum Dialogue highlighted the need for African-led responses to evolving security challenges. The discussions underscored a shared message: lasting peace requires more than dialogue alone. It also depends on effective African leadership, stronger cooperation, sustainable financing and a sustained commitment to solutions that reflect the continent's priorities and realities. ethiopia.title: TPLF Warns Against Movement Around Tigray Airports, Rejects Caretaker Administration
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: TPLF Warns Against Movement Around Tigray Airports, Rejects Caretaker Administration - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: TPLF Warns Against Movement Around Tigray Airports, Rejects Caretaker Administration 17 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) has warned residents against movement around airports in Tigray, alleging that the Ethiopian federal government is using aviation facilities for military purposes, while rejecting the newly established caretaker administration as illegitimate. In a statement issued on Friday, 16 October, the TPLF described the administration appointed by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government as a "Prosperity structure" imposed on the region and declared that decisions made under its authority would have "no legality or enforceability." The party further warned that institutions cooperating with the administration would be considered part of the ruling Prosperity Party and held accountable, escalating its opposition to the federal government's intervention in the region. The federal government announced the six-month caretaker administration on 16 October, assigning officials responsibility for administration and public services, economic affairs and reconstruction, peace and security, and political organization. Dr. Shishay Amare was also appointed mayor of Mekelle. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines According to the announcement from the prime minister's office, the administration, which didn't name the interim president or administrator, is intended to restore public services, address security challenges, facilitate the return of internally displaced people and prepare the region for elections. Its mandate also includes rebuilding government institutions and rehabilitating infrastructure damaged during the war. The TPLF, however, disputed the legitimacy of the arrangement, arguing that the appointees lacked the authority to administer Tigray. TPLF raises airport security concerns The TPLF's statement alleged that the federal government was diverting airport facilities from civilian transportation to military operations, claiming this threatened the population's survival. "Therefore, we strictly warn that no movement of any kind should take place around the airport," the statement said. The party did not identify specific military operations or provide independently verifiable evidence supporting the allegation. The warning comes amid renewed fighting and heightened security concerns in Tigray, where control of key towns and infrastructure has become part of the broader conflict. The TPLF also alleged that unidentified forces were conducting surveillance by using three-wheeled vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles and other means of transport to move between towns and rural areas. It said the allegations had been confirmed through individuals taken into custody, but did not provide further details that could independently establish the claims. ethiopia.title: Kenya Overtakes Ethiopia As East Africa's Largest Economy in Dollar Terms, IMF Estimates Show
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Kenya Overtakes Ethiopia As East Africa's Largest Economy in Dollar Terms, IMF Estimates Show - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Kenya Overtakes Ethiopia As East Africa's Largest Economy in Dollar Terms, IMF Estimates Show 17 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Kenya has overtaken Ethiopia as Eastern Africa's largest economy measured by nominal gross domestic product (GDP) in US dollar terms, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), a shift largely attributed to exchange-rate movements rather than faster real economic growth. The IMF's estimates show Ethiopia's economy continuing to expand more rapidly in real terms, even as the depreciation of the birr reduced the dollar value of its output. Kenya's comparatively stronger currency performance, alongside continued economic growth, helped increase the value of its economy when measured in US dollars. According to the IMF's October 2026 WEO estimates, Ethiopia's real GDP grew by 9.2% in 2025, compared with 4.6% in Kenya. The Fund projects Ethiopia's economy to expand by 9.2% in 2026 and 7.8% in 2027, while Kenya's growth is projected at 4.5% and 4.7%, respectively. The figures underscore the distinction between nominal GDP, which values economic output at prevailing market exchange rates, and real GDP growth, which measures changes in output after accounting for price changes. A country's dollar-denominated GDP can decline sharply following currency depreciation even when its domestic production is increasing. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Ethiopia's currency shift followed the government's July 2024 move toward a more market-determined exchange-rate system, a key component of its economic reform programme supported by an approximately US$3.4 billion IMF Extended Credit Facility. The subsequent depreciation of the birr substantially reduced the dollar value of the country's economic output. Kenya's economy, meanwhile, benefited from a stronger shilling, which increased the dollar valuation of its output. The IMF estimates indicate that Kenya's nominal GDP in US dollar terms increased by about 13.7% in 2025, while Ethiopia's dollar-denominated GDP fell sharply from its 2024 level. The change in ranking reflects the combined effects of economic growth, inflation and exchange-rate movements on the dollar value of each economy. The IMF estimates nominal GDP per capita at about US$1,130 in Ethiopia and US$2,790 in Kenya in 2026, illustrating the difference between the total size of an economy and output per person. Inflation also remains a concern. The IMF projects average consumer price inflation of approximately 11.7% in Ethiopia in 2026, compared with about 6% in Kenya. Persistent price pressures, alongside exchange-rate changes, affect households' purchasing power and the cost of imports. While Ethiopia's real GDP grew by 9.2% in 2025, Kenya's growth was only 4.6%. The depreciation of the Ethiopian birr, following a shift to a market-determined exchange-rate system, significantly reduced the dollar value of its economy. In contrast, Kenya's stronger shilling contributed to a 13.7% increase in its nominal GDP in dollar terms. The IMF projects continued growth for both economies, with Ethiopia expected to maintain higher real GDP growth rates compared to Kenya. The nominal GDP per capita is estimated at $1,130 for Ethiopia and $2,790 for Kenya in 2026.

ethiopia.title: Eritrea Asks AU to Restore Representation After Ethiopia Expels Diplomats
ethiopia.content: Africa: Eritrea Asks AU to Restore Representation After Ethiopia Expels Diplomats - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Africa: Eritrea Asks AU to Restore Representation After Ethiopia Expels Diplomats 15 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Eritrea has urged the African Union (AU) to take urgent measures to restore its representation at the organization's headquarters in Addis Abeba, saying Ethiopia's expulsion of 10 Eritrean diplomats has effectively deprived the country of its rights to participate in the continental body's activities. In a letter dated October 12, 2026, and addressed to the AU Commission's Bureau of the Chairperson, Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the October 1 decision by the Ethiopian government to declare 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata included its chargé d'affaires en pied, who also serves as the country's permanent representative to the AU and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), as well as all three diplomatic staff assigned to cover the two institutions. "By expelling the Permanent Representative and the entire diplomatic staff assigned to participate in AU and ECA, the Ethiopian Government has effectively deprived the State of Eritrea of its fundamental rights as a Member State to be represented at the AU and UNECA and to participate in their activities," the letter stated. Eritrea said its chargé d'affaires had verbally notified the AU Commission's deputy chairperson of the matter on October 2, after being unable to reach the chairperson. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The ministry argued that Ethiopia's decision violated the AU's founding principles and international agreements governing the organization's headquarters in Addis Abeba. It cited Article 4(a) of the AU Constitutive Act, which establishes the sovereign equality of member states, and Article 15 of the AU Headquarters Agreement, which guarantees diplomatic privileges, immunities and facilities for accredited representatives. The letter also cited the 1965 General Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the Organization of African Unity, arguing that the expulsion obstructed Eritrea's ability to carry out its official mandate at the AU headquarters. "Eritrea's statutory rights of membership in the African Union cannot be curtailed or compromised at the whim of another Member State," the ministry said. Eritrea called on the AU Commission to bring the matter urgently before the organization's Executive Council and Assembly, urging them to take "immediate corrective measures" to restore its representation and ensure its full participation as a sovereign and equal member. The diplomatic dispute follows a sharp deterioration in relations between Addis Abeba and Asmara. On October 1, Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats based at the Eritrean Embassy in Addis Abeba and the country's permanent mission to the AU and UNECA persona non grata, ordering them to leave within 48 hours. Ethiopia accused the diplomats of activities threatening national security and violating the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, amid renewed tensions over the conflict in Ethiopia's Tigray region. Eritrea rejected the allegations as unwarranted and subsequently announced that it would sever all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia. Asmara accused Addis Abeba of pursuing a sustained campaign of hostility linked to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's stated ambition to secure sovereign access to the Red Sea. The Ethiopian government's actions followed its closure of its embassy in Asmara in August 2026, further undermining diplomatic channels between the two neighboring countries. The dispute also raises questions about the distinction between bilateral diplomatic relations and the rights of AU member states to maintain representation at the organization's headquarters. In its October 12 letter, Eritrea argued that while the opening and operation of embassies are governed by bilateral arrangements and international diplomatic law, a host country cannot unilaterally determine whether another AU member state may exercise its membership rights within the continental organization. Diplomatic relations had been strained for years The latest confrontation follows years of fragile diplomatic engagement after the 2018 rapprochement between Abiy and Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki , which formally ended two decades of hostility following Eritrea's 1993 independence and the 1998-2000 border war. In July 2018, the two leaders signed a Joint Declaration of Peace and Friendship in Asmara, opening the way for the restoration of diplomatic relations and the exchange of ambassadors. Ethiopia appointed Redwan Hussein as its ambassador to Eritrea, while Eritrea appointed former education minister Semere Russom as its ambassador to Ethiopia in the same year. However, the renewed diplomatic relations yielded little substantive progress beyond paving the way for a devastating two-year war in Ethiopia's Tigray region, during which Ethiopian and Eritrean forces fought alongside one another against Tigrayan forces. Both countries' forces have been accused of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the conflict. The rapprochement proved fragile even before the war formally ended. In April 2022, Addis Standard reported that Eritrea had replaced its ambassador to Ethiopia, Semere Russom, with Biniam Berhe as chargé d'affaires en pied, a diplomatic designation indicating that the post of ambassador was to remain permanently vacant . Biniam presented his credentials to Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials on March 30, 2022. His appointment followed earlier difficulties in establishing full ambassadorial representation between the two countries, with the credentials of previous Ethiopian envoys reportedly left unaccepted or delayed . The developments signaled that diplomatic ties remained constrained even after the 2018 peace declaration, with both sides struggling to establish stable, fully functioning ambassadorial relations. Relations have since deteriorated further following Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's public statements on Ethiopia's quest for Red Sea access and, more recently, the resurgence of conflict in northern Ethiopia . Eritrea's latest appeal to the AU now places the dispute before the continental organization, whose headquarters are in Addis Abeba, Ethiopia's capital. ethiopia.summary: Eritrea has requested the African Union (AU) to restore its representation at the organization's headquarters in Addis Ababa after Ethiopia expelled ten Eritrean diplomats, including its chargé d'affaires, on October 1, 2026. Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs argued that this expulsion deprived the country of its rights as a member state to participate in AU activities, violating the AU's founding principles and international agreements. The letter, sent on October 12, emphasized that Ethiopia's actions obstructed Eritrea's ability to fulfill its diplomatic mandate. The diplomatic rift follows a deterioration in relations between the two countries, exacerbated by Ethiopia's accusations of national security threats against the diplomats and Eritrea's subsequent severing of ties. Eritrea called for urgent corrective measures from the AU to ensure its full participation as a sovereign member.

somalia.title: Turkish Ambassador Visits Aden Adde Airport as Favori Highlights Expansion to 1 Million Passenger Capacity - FTL Somalia
somalia.summary: Turkish Ambassador to Somalia, Mehmet Yılmaz, visited Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu to discuss ongoing expansion efforts. The airport is set to increase its passenger capacity to 1 million annually, a significant upgrade aimed at enhancing air travel in the region. During the visit, Ambassador Yılmaz emphasized the importance of the expansion for improving connectivity and supporting economic growth in Somalia. The project is part of broader Turkish investments in the country, reflecting a commitment to strengthening bilateral relations. The ambassador's visit underscores Turkey's role in Somalia's development and infrastructure improvements.

somalia.title: Somalia beat Rwanda on penalties to reach CECAFA U-17 final - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Somalia triumphed over Rwanda in a tense penalty shootout to secure a place in the CECAFA U-17 final. The match ended in a draw after regulation and extra time, leading to penalties where Somalia emerged victorious. This win marks a significant achievement for the Somali U-17 team, showcasing their resilience and skill in a competitive tournament. The final will see Somalia compete for the championship title, further highlighting the progress of youth football in the region.

somalia.title: Families fleeing Somalia crises find bleak prospects in Dadaab refugee camps - Radio Ergo
somalia.summary: Families fleeing crises in Somalia are facing dire conditions in the Dadaab refugee camps in Kenya. The camps, originally established to accommodate 90,000 people, now house over 200,000 refugees, leading to overcrowding and inadequate resources. Many families have escaped violence, drought, and famine, but upon arrival, they encounter limited access to food, healthcare, and education. The situation is exacerbated by insufficient aid and funding, leaving many refugees in a state of uncertainty and despair. Despite the challenges, some families remain hopeful for a better future, while others struggle to meet their basic needs in the harsh camp environment. The ongoing humanitarian crisis highlights the urgent need for increased support and sustainable solutions for displaced populations.

somalia.title: Ilhan Omar Is the Right Kind of American. Trump Is the Wrong Kind. - The New Republic
somalia.summary: The article contrasts Ilhan Omar and Donald Trump, arguing that Omar embodies the values of inclusivity and diversity that define American identity, while Trump represents a divisive and exclusionary approach. It highlights Omar's background as a Somali refugee and her commitment to social justice, which resonate with the ideals of the American Dream. In contrast, Trump's rhetoric and policies are depicted as fostering division and undermining the principles of equality and acceptance. The piece emphasizes the importance of embracing diverse narratives in America, suggesting that Omar's perspective is essential for a more equitable society, while Trump's stance is seen as detrimental to the nation's core values.

somalia.title: OIC reaffirms support for Somalia’s territorial integrity during talks in Baghdad - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has reiterated its commitment to Somalia's territorial integrity during discussions held in Baghdad. The meeting focused on various issues affecting the region, with member states expressing solidarity with Somalia amid ongoing challenges. The OIC emphasized the importance of unity and cooperation among member nations to support Somalia's stability and development. Participants highlighted the need for a collective approach to address security concerns and promote peace in the country. The reaffirmation of support comes as Somalia continues to navigate complex political and security landscapes, with the OIC pledging to assist in efforts aimed at strengthening the nation's sovereignty and territorial claims.

somalia.title: Somalia’s Opposition Alliance to Hold Key Political Talks in Nairobi, Kenya - Garowe Online
somalia.summary: Somalia's opposition alliance is set to convene crucial political talks in Nairobi, Kenya, aimed at addressing ongoing political challenges in the country. The discussions will involve key opposition leaders who are seeking to unify their stance and strategize on pressing issues, including the upcoming elections and governance concerns. This meeting is seen as a significant step towards fostering collaboration among opposition groups and enhancing their influence in the political landscape of Somalia. The alliance aims to present a united front to advocate for democratic reforms and address the grievances of the Somali populace. The outcome of these talks could have substantial implications for Somalia's political future.

somalia.title: Fisheries Minister Meets Turkish Envoy to Deepen Blue Economy Cooperation - FTL Somalia
somalia.summary: Fisheries Minister of Somalia met with the Turkish Ambassador to Somalia to enhance collaboration in the blue economy sector. The discussions focused on strengthening partnerships in fisheries management, sustainable practices, and investment opportunities. Both parties expressed a commitment to improving the livelihoods of coastal communities through effective resource management and technological advancements. The meeting underscored the importance of international cooperation in addressing challenges faced by the fisheries sector and promoting sustainable development. The Turkish envoy highlighted Turkey's readiness to support Somalia in achieving its blue economy goals.

somalia.title: Somalia plans unified digital government platform built around national ID - Biometric Update
somalia.summary: Somalia is set to develop a unified digital government platform centered on a national identification system. This initiative aims to enhance public service delivery and streamline government operations by integrating various services into a single digital framework. The platform will utilize biometric data to create a secure and efficient identification process for citizens, facilitating access to essential services. The government emphasizes that this move is crucial for improving transparency and accountability within public institutions. By establishing a comprehensive digital identity system, Somalia seeks to bolster its governance and foster economic development, ultimately benefiting its citizens.

somalia.title: Somalia, Türkiye discuss cooperation on fisheries and blue economy - Shabelle Media Network
somalia.summary: Somalia and Türkiye have engaged in discussions to enhance cooperation in the fisheries sector and the broader blue economy. The talks were held during a meeting between Somali Minister of Fisheries and Marine Resources, Abdirahman Mohamed, and Türkiye's Ambassador to Somalia, Melih Karalar. Both parties emphasized the importance of sustainable fishing practices and the potential for economic growth through the development of marine resources. The discussions aimed to strengthen bilateral relations and explore opportunities for investment and technical assistance in Somalia's fisheries industry. This collaboration is seen as a vital step towards improving food security and economic stability in Somalia.

somalia.title: Somalia and Iraq discuss expanding trade and livestock exports - Shabelle Media Network
somalia.summary: Somalia and Iraq have initiated discussions aimed at enhancing trade relations and increasing livestock exports. The talks focus on potential agreements that would facilitate the export of Somali livestock to Iraq, which has expressed interest in sourcing livestock from Somalia. Both countries are exploring ways to strengthen economic ties and improve bilateral trade, recognizing the mutual benefits of such cooperation. The discussions reflect a broader effort to diversify trade partnerships and boost the agricultural sector in Somalia, while providing Iraq with access to quality livestock.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من مجموعات دوري الأبطال - مانكيش نت
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا. جاء ذلك بعد الأداء القوي الذي قدمه الفريقان في المباريات التمهيدية. الهلال السوداني حقق نتائج إيجابية في مبارياته السابقة، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل، بينما تمكن السويحلي من تقديم عرض قوي في التصفيات. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق النجاح في المرحلة المقبلة من البطولة، حيث تعتبر هذه المنافسة فرصة كبيرة لإظهار مهاراتهم على المستوى القاري.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من دور المجموعات في دوري ابطال افريقيا - Elsport
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال إفريقيا بعد أدائهما الجيد في التصفيات. حيث حقق الهلال السوداني فوزًا مهمًا في مباراته الأخيرة، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل. من جهة أخرى، قدم السويحلي الليبي أداءً قويًا في مواجهاته، مما جعله قريبًا من تحقيق نفس الهدف. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى استكمال مشوارهما بنجاح في البطولة القارية، حيث تعتبر هذه المرحلة حاسمة في مسيرتهما.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يحسم مواجهة سيداما بونا ويقترب من التأهل الأفريقي - اخبار السودان
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزًا مهمًا على سيداما بونا الإثيوبي في مباراة ضمن تصفيات دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يقربه من التأهل للمرحلة التالية. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، حيث سجل الأهداف كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة. قدم الفريق أداءً قويًا خلال المباراة، مما ساهم في تعزيز فرصه في المنافسة على اللقب الأفريقي. بهذا الفوز، يواصل الهلال مسيرته الناجحة في البطولة ويعزز من موقفه في المجموعة.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تقام اليوم مواجهة مرتقبة بين فريق الهلال وسيداما، حيث ينتظر عشاق كرة القدم هذه المباراة بفارغ الصبر. ستبدأ المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. سيتم بث اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات، منها القناة الرياضية السعودية، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر على الإنترنت. يُعتبر هذا اللقاء مهمًا للفريقين، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز لتعزيز موقفه في البطولة، بينما يأمل سيداما في تقديم أداء قوي أمام خصمهم.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تستعد جماهير كرة القدم لمتابعة مواجهة الهلال وسيداما اليوم، حيث من المقرر أن تنطلق المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. ستقام المباراة في إطار المنافسات القارية، مما يزيد من حماس المشجعين. يمكن متابعة اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات ناقلة، منها قناة "SSC" التي تمتلك حقوق البث، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر. يُتوقع أن تكون المباراة مثيرة، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز وتعزيز موقفه في البطولة.

football.title: السويحلي يسقط الترجي وتعادل صنداونز.. نتائج ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا - يلاكورة
football.summary: حقق فريق السويحلي فوزًا مهمًا على الترجي التونسي في ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يعزز آماله في التأهل للدور المقبل. في مباراة أخرى، انتهت مواجهة صنداونز الجنوب أفريقي مع منافسه بالتعادل، مما يجعل الأمور مفتوحة في مباراة الإياب. تأتي هذه النتائج في إطار المنافسات القوية التي يشهدها دوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث يسعى كل فريق لتحقيق أفضل أداء لضمان التأهل.

football.title: مدرب الهلال يتوعد سيداما ويثق في بلوغ مجموعات دوري الأبطال - winwin
football.summary: مدرب الهلال، رامون دياز، أعرب عن ثقته في قدرة فريقه على تجاوز عقبة سيداما الإثيوبي في التصفيات المؤهلة لدوري أبطال آسيا. خلال مؤتمر صحفي، أكد دياز أن الهلال يمتلك الإمكانيات اللازمة لتحقيق الفوز والتأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. وأشار إلى أهمية المباراة وضرورة التركيز على الأداء الجيد، مشددًا على أن الفريق جاهز تمامًا لمواجهة التحديات. كما أعرب عن تفاؤله بقدرة اللاعبين على تقديم مستوى مميز يضمن لهم النجاح في هذه المرحلة الحاسمة.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يقترب من مجموعات الأبطال بثنائية.. ومولودية الجزائر في ورطة - الجمهور الإخباري
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على ضيفه مولودية الجزائر بنتيجة 2-0 في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. بهذا الانتصار، اقترب الهلال من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات، حيث قدم أداءً قوياً واستطاع تسجيل هدفين في الشوط الثاني. في المقابل، يواجه مولودية الجزائر تحديات كبيرة بعد هذه الخسارة، مما يزيد من ضغوط الفريق قبل مباراة الإياب. يحتاج الفريق الجزائري إلى تحقيق نتيجة إيجابية في المباراة القادمة لضمان فرصه في التأهل.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يضرب في إثيوبيا ويقترب من مجموعات أبطال أفريقيا - السودان اليوم
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على مضيفه فاسيل كيتيما الإثيوبي في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. سجل أهداف الهلال كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة، حيث قدم الفريق أداءً مميزاً خلال اللقاء. ومن المقرر أن تقام مباراة الإياب في السودان، حيث يسعى الهلال إلى تأكيد تفوقه وضمان التأهل. يعتبر هذا الفوز خطوة إيجابية نحو تحقيق طموحات الفريق في البطولة الأفريقية.

football.title: أبطال إفريقيا.. الهلال السوداني يقترب من دور المجموعات وخسارة المريخ أمام حوريا - إرم نيوز
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني من التأهل إلى دور المجموعات في بطولة دوري أبطال إفريقيا بعد فوزه على فريق ريفرز يونايتد النيجيري في مباراة الذهاب. بينما تعرض فريق المريخ السوداني لهزيمة أمام حوريا كوناكري الغيني، مما يعقد موقفه في المنافسة. الهلال قدم أداءً قويًا، مما يعزز آماله في الوصول إلى المرحلة التالية، بينما يحتاج المريخ إلى تحسين أدائه في المباريات القادمة لتفادي الخروج المبكر من البطولة.
